help me connect my spotify to bluetooth on debian 13  desktop (KDE plasma 6)

Good — I’ll give a short step‑by‑step you can follow, plus a few quick troubleshooting commands. I’ll cover both GUI (KDE) and terminal ways and include fixes for PipeWire (likely on Debian 13) and PulseAudio setups.

Before you start: put your Bluetooth headphones/speaker into pairing mode.

1) Make sure required packages & services are present
Open a terminal and run:
- Update package list:
  sudo apt update
- Install common Bluetooth + audio packages for KDE/PipeWire:
  sudo apt install bluez bluedevil wireplumber pipewire pipewire-pulse libspa-0.2-bluetooth pavucontrol

(If you prefer Blueman or extra tools: sudo apt install blueman. If your system still uses PulseAudio instead of PipeWire, install pulseaudio-module-bluetooth instead of pipewire-pulse.)

Enable/start Bluetooth:
  sudo systemctl enable --now bluetooth

Restart user audio services (PipeWire):
  systemctl --user restart pipewire wireplumber pipewire-pulse

2) Pair & connect the device (GUI)
- Open KDE System Settings > Bluetooth (or click the tray Bluetooth icon).
- Click “Search” / “Add device”. When your headphones appear, click Pair, then Connect.
- After pairing, right‑click the device in the list and choose “Connect to Audio Sink” (or similar).

Or pair via terminal:
  bluetoothctl
  # in bluetoothctl prompt:
  power on
  scan on
  # wait until you see your device MAC (XX:XX:...)
  pair XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX
  trust XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX
  connect XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX
  exit

3) Select the Bluetooth sink as audio output
- Quick GUI: System Settings > Audio > Output Devices — select your Bluetooth device and set it as default.
- Or use pavucontrol (install if needed). Open it while Spotify is playing: Playback tab → find the Spotify stream → choose the Bluetooth device from the dropdown.

Terminal:
- List sinks:
  pactl list short sinks
- Set default sink:
  pactl set-default-sink <SINK_NAME>
- Move running Spotify stream (find stream index first):
  pactl list short sink-inputs
  pactl move-sink-input <INPUT_INDEX> <SINK_NAME>

Note: pactl works with PulseAudio and with PipeWire when pipewire-pulse is active.

4) Per‑app routing in KDE
- System Settings > Audio > Application Streams (or Playback) while Spotify is playing lets you set the stream to your Bluetooth device.

5) Troubleshooting
- Check Bluetooth service:
  systemctl status bluetooth
- Check paired devices:
  bluetoothctl devices
- If the device pairs but no audio, ensure libspa-0.2-bluetooth (PipeWire) or pulseaudio-module-bluetooth (PulseAudio) is installed.
- Restart user audio services:
  systemctl --user restart wireplumber pipewire pipewire-pulse
- For PulseAudio only:
  pactl load-module module-bluetooth-discover
- If Spotify was installed as Flatpak: flatpak apps normally use the host audio automatically; but if you used a sandboxed package and you still don’t see the device, tell me how Spotify was installed (deb, Flatpak, Snap) and I’ll give specific fixes.

If you try these steps and it still won’t play, tell me:
- output of: pactl list short sinks
- output of: bluetoothctl devices
- how Spotify was installed (deb/Flatpak/snap)
I’ll help you from there.
